title: Verify protection: term life, disability, umbrella
summary: Already addressed in Phase 2 if you started fresh; revisit here as your income and net worth grow.
detailsHtml:
Why this gets revisited

The protection layer scales with what you have to protect. As wealth grows, liability exposure grows. As family responsibilities accumulate, life insurance needs grow. Disability coverage should be reviewed when income changes materially.

Estate planning baseline

At minimum: a will, a healthcare proxy / advance directive, durable power of attorney for finances, and updated beneficiary designations on all retirement accounts and life insurance. Beneficiary designations override your will, so they must be kept current — divorce and remarriage are the most common failure points.

Annual gift tax exclusion (2026): $19,000 per recipient. You can give up to $19,000 to any number of recipients each year without triggering gift tax reporting or eating into your $15M lifetime exemption. Married couples can split gifts to give $38,000 per recipient. For families with substantial assets, systematic annual gifting compounds into meaningful estate reduction over decades — $19,000/year to each of three children over 20 years moves $1.14M out of the estate without using lifetime exemption at all.
Cost benchmark: Basic estate documents from an attorney run $500–$2,500 in most U.S. markets. Online services (Trust & Will, FreeWill, LegalZoom) handle simple cases for $100–$300. Both are vastly cheaper than dying intestate.
